title: Preserving Language Models under One-Shot Pruning
question: With no retraining and no gradient step, decide which half of a pretrained LM's weights to remove and what values the survivors take.
elab:
Removing weights changes the role of those that survive; the task seeks a one-shot importance and compensation rule that preserves language-model predictions after half or more of the weights are pruned, without retraining.

A large fixed fraction of a pretrained language model's weights has to go in a single pass, with no retraining and no gradient step. SparseGPT, Wanda and RIA each answer "which weights?" with a different importance score and a different rule for what the surviving weights should be set to, and their relative order depends on the sparsity level and pattern. The task asks for the criterion itself, evaluated on OPT at 50% and 70% unstructured sparsity (the high-sparsity regime where the data-free criteria collapse) and at 2:4. It matters because one-shot pruning is the only kind that is affordable at frontier scale, and the criterion is the entire method.
readme_settings_line: OPT-125M · 50% unstructured; OPT-1.3B · 70% unstructured; OPT-1.3B · 2:4 semi-structured.
readme_methods_line: Wanda (Sun et al., 2024); RIA (Zhang et al., 2024); SparseGPT (Frantar & Alistarh, 2023); Magnitude pruning; RIA relative importance only (Zhang et al., 2024); Random mask.
description_md:
# Which Weights Should a One-Shot Sparsifier Remove

## Research Question

A large, fixed fraction of the weights of a pretrained language model has to
go, in one pass, with no retraining and no gradient step. **Which weights, and
what should the survivors be set to?**

You design the per-weight importance rule, the group its scores are compared
within, and — if you want one — the correction applied to the weights that stay.
The sparsity budget and the sparsity pattern are fixed by the harness and are the
same for every method.

## Background

For a linear layer computing `y = x W^T`, removing a weight perturbs the layer's
output. The literature disagrees about what makes a weight expendable, and the
disagreement is sharp enough to be settled empirically.

**Magnitude** takes `|W_ij|`: small weights move the output little. It needs no
data at all.

Frantar and Alistarh (*SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can Be Accurately
Pruned in One-Shot*, ICML 2023, arXiv:2301.00774) start instead from the
second-order expansion of the layerwise reconstruction error under the Hessian
`H = 2 X X^T` of the layer's own inputs. Their criterion for the weight in column
`c` is `w_c^2 / [H^{-1}]_{cc}^2`, and — this is the part that distinguishes them
from a pure score — after each column is pruned the error it caused is
**propagated into the columns not yet visited**, so the surviving weights absorb
what the removed ones were doing. Their Algorithm 1 selects the mask for `B_s =
128` columns at a time with a lazy weight-update block of `B = 128` and a Hessian
dampening of 1% of the mean diagonal.

Sun, Liu, Bair and Kolter (*A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large
Language Models*, ICLR 2024, arXiv:2306.11695) argue the inverse Hessian is not
needed. Their metric is `S_ij = |W_ij| · ||X_j||_2` (their Eq. 1), the weight
scaled by the norm of the activations it consumes, and they make a second,
independent claim: the *comparison group* matters as much as the score. They
compare weights only among those feeding the same output neuron — "for a weight
`W_ij` that connects input `j` to output `i`, we define the comparison group for
this weight as all weights connecting to output `i`" (their Eq. 2) — and report
that this is consistently better than one threshold for the whole matrix, for
their metric *and* for plain magnitude. They perform no weight update at all.

Zhang, Bai, Lin, Zhao, Hou and Cannistraci (*Plug-and-Play: An Efficient
Post-training Pruning Method for Large Language Models*, ICLR 2024, OpenReview
`Tr0lPx9woF`) object that both of the above let a weight's fate be decided by the
scale of its row or column rather than by its role. They normalise first —
Relative Importance, their Eq. 2:

    RI_ij = |W_ij| / sum_i |W_ij|  +  |W_ij| / sum_j |W_ij|

— and then reintroduce activations with a tunable exponent, their Eq. 3:
`RIA_ij = RI_ij · (||X_j||_2)^a`, selecting `a = 0.5`. They score with a single
threshold over the whole matrix.

So the field offers three axes that are usually varied together and rarely
separated: what the score is, what it is compared against, and whether the
surviving weights are corrected. Untangling them is the question here.

## What You Can Modify

`wanda/mlsb_prune/custom_pruner.py`, the `LayerPruner` class inside the marked
editable region:

```python
def prune(self, W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta) -> (mask, W_new)
    # W           float32 [m, n]  the layer's dense weight, y = x @ W.T
    # scaler_row  float32 [n]     mean over calibration batches of the squared
    #                             l2 norm of each input channel's activations
    # H           float32 [n, n]  (2/N) * sum_b X_b X_b^T over the same batches;
    #                             note torch.diag(H) == 2 * scaler_row
    # cfg         dict            {"sparsity", "prune_n", "prune_m"}
    # mask        bool  [m, n]    True = remove this weight
    # W_new       float32 [m, n]  what the survivors should be, or None to keep W
```

Called once per linear layer, inside `torch.no_grad()`, on GPU tensors. `torch`
and `math` are available; there is no network, no file writing, and no access to
the evaluation data. A selection helper covering the row-wise, matrix-wise and
N:M comparison groups is provided as fixed code above the editable region — use
it or write your own; only the mask you return counts.

## What The Harness Does With What You Return

Blocks are visited in order. For each layer the fixed pipeline installs
`W_new.masked_fill(mask, 0)`, and then **re-runs the block so every later block
sees the activations of the already-pruned model** — your decision for one layer
changes the statistics the next one is scored on. This is the reference
construction, not a simplification of it. The finished weights are written to an
artifact that a separate process reloads and scores.

## Sparsity Budget

`cfg["sparsity"]` of **each** layer's weights must be removed, to within a small
tolerance in both directions: you choose which weights, never how many, and never
how the budget is divided between layers. When `cfg["prune_n"] > 0` the mask must
additionally remove at least `prune_n` of every `prune_m` consecutive input
channels, independently per output row. Both constraints are re-derived from the
stored mask by the evaluator, out of process, which also checks the weights are
genuinely zero wherever the mask removes one; a run that misses either constraint
on any layer produces **no metric at all**. Writing a zero into a position the
mask did *not* remove is allowed — it costs you accuracy, not budget.

## Fixed Pipeline

Fixed and identical for every method: which linear layers are pruned, the
calibration corpus and the number and length of the windows drawn from it, the
two calibration statistics and how they are accumulated, the order in which
blocks are visited, the re-run rule above, the sparsity target and pattern, the
storage format and the evaluation. Embeddings, normalisation layers, the
positional table and the output head are never pruned. The fixed code is provided
as read-only context: `run_prune.py`, `pipeline.py`, `storage.py` and
`modelio.py`.

## Reference Baselines

* **Unmodified starter** — `|W_ij|`, one threshold for the whole weight matrix.
  Weight-only; it never looks at the calibration statistics.
* **Random** — an i.i.d. uniform score spending exactly the same budget with no
  information.
* **Wanda** — `|W_ij| · ||X_j||_2`, compared within each output row
  (Sun et al., ICLR 2024, Eq. 1 and Eq. 2).
* **Relative Importance alone** — `|W_ij|/sum_i|W_ij| + |W_ij|/sum_j|W_ij|`, one
  threshold for the whole matrix; the ablation the RIA paper reports (its
  Table 2, row `RI`) to separate the normalisation from the activation term. It
  uses no calibration data.
* **RIA** — `(|W_ij|/sum_i|W_ij| + |W_ij|/sum_j|W_ij|) · (||X_j||_2)^a` with
  `a = 0.5`, one threshold for the whole matrix (Zhang et al., ICLR 2024,
  Eq. 2-3; `a = 0.5` is the released default).
* **SparseGPT** — OBS mask selection on `w_c^2 / [H^{-1}]_{cc}^2` with sequential
  error propagation into the unvisited columns, `blocksize = 128`, Hessian
  dampening `0.01` (Frantar & Alistarh, ICML 2023, Algorithm 1). The only
  reference here that changes the surviving weights.

## Metric

Perplexity of the pruned model on a held-out English corpus, **lower is
better**, computed by a separate process that reloads the pruned weights from the
stored artifact. Several sparsity settings are evaluated; the task score combines
them so that a weak one cannot be offset by a strong one. `sparsity`, `layers` and `prune_seconds` are reported
alongside but are not scored.

"""Which weights should a one-shot sparsifier remove, and what should the ones
that survive be set to?

You design `LayerPruner.prune`. Everything else -- which layers are pruned, the
calibration corpus and its sampling, the two calibration statistics, the order in
which blocks are visited, the sparsity budget, the sparsity pattern, the storage
format and the evaluation -- is fixed and shared by every method.

WHAT THE HARNESS DOES WITH WHAT YOU RETURN
------------------------------------------
For each linear layer of each decoder block, in order, the fixed pipeline

    1. runs the calibration corpus through the block and collects, for that
       layer, `scaler_row` and `H` (below);
    2. calls `self.prune(W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta)` once;
    3. applies `W_final = W_new.masked_fill(mask, 0)` and installs it;
    4. re-runs the block, so every later block sees the activations of the
       ALREADY-PRUNED model -- your decision for layer k changes the statistics
       layer k+1 is scored on;
    5. writes the finished weights to an artifact. A separate process, which
       never imports this file, reloads that artifact, re-derives the sparsity of
       every layer, and computes the perplexity that is scored.

CONTRACT
--------
`prune(W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta) -> (mask, W_new)`

    W           float32 [m, n]  the layer's dense weight (a copy; m outputs,
                                n input channels). `y = x @ W.T`.
    scaler_row  float32 [n]     mean over calibration batches of the squared
                                l2 norm of each input channel's activations.
    H           float32 [n, n]  the layerwise second-moment matrix
                                (2/N) * sum_b X_b X_b^T over the same batches.
                                Note `torch.diag(H) == 2 * scaler_row`.
    cfg         dict            {"sparsity", "prune_n", "prune_m"} -- fixed by
                                the harness, never by you.
    meta        dict            {"name", "block", "layer", "m", "n", "seed",
                                "model"}.

    mask        bool  [m, n]    True = remove this weight.
    W_new       float32 [m, n]  what the surviving weights should be. Return
                                `None` to keep the original values; return a
                                tensor to compensate for what was removed.

Called inside `torch.no_grad()` on GPU tensors. `torch` and `math` are
available. There is no network, no evaluation data, and nothing outside this
call to write state into that the evaluator will read.

BUDGET -- the same for every method, and enforced out of process
---------------------------------------------------------------
Your mask must remove `cfg["sparsity"]` of EACH layer's weights, to within a
small tolerance in BOTH directions. You choose WHICH weights, never HOW MANY,
and never how the budget is split between layers. When `cfg["prune_n"] > 0` the
mask must additionally remove at least `prune_n` of every `prune_m` CONSECUTIVE
input channels, independently for each output row. A run that misses either
constraint on any layer produces no metric at all.

The budget is the MASK, not the zeros: the mask is stored alongside the weights
and the evaluator checks both that it meets the budget and that the weights are
genuinely zero wherever it removes one. Writing a zero into a position the mask
did not remove is allowed and only costs you accuracy.
"""

import math

import torch


# ==============================================================================
# FIXED -- selection helpers. Call them or write your own; the mask you return is
# what counts.
# ==============================================================================

def select_by_metric(W_metric, sparsity, prune_n, prune_m, per_output_row=True):
    """Remove the lowest-scoring weights under the requested pattern.

    `per_output_row=True` compares scores only among the weights feeding one
    output neuron (`sparsity` of each ROW is removed); `False` compares them
    across the whole matrix (`sparsity` of the TENSOR is removed). Both are used
    in the literature and the choice is part of the method, not of the harness.

    When `prune_n > 0` the comparison group is instead each block of `prune_m`
    consecutive input channels within a row, and `per_output_row` is ignored.

    In every case EXACTLY the budgeted number of weights is removed from each
    group, with ties broken by index. That matters: a metric can be exactly zero
    for a whole input channel -- OPT's `fc2` reads a post-ReLU activation, so a
    channel that never fires has zero activation norm -- and a plain
    `metric <= threshold` rule would then remove an unbounded number of extra
    weights and miss the budget.
    """
    W_mask = torch.zeros_like(W_metric, dtype=torch.bool)
    if prune_n > 0:
        for ii in range(0, W_metric.shape[1], prune_m):
            tmp = W_metric[:, ii:(ii + prune_m)].float()
            idx = torch.topk(tmp, prune_n, dim=1, largest=False)[1]
            W_mask.scatter_(1, ii + idx, True)
        return W_mask
    if per_output_row:
        order = torch.sort(W_metric, dim=-1, stable=True)[1]
        keep = int(W_metric.shape[1] * sparsity)
        W_mask.scatter_(1, order[:, :keep], True)
        return W_mask
    flat = W_metric.flatten().float()
    k = int(flat.numel() * sparsity)
    flat_mask = torch.zeros_like(flat, dtype=torch.bool)
    if k > 0:
        flat_mask[torch.argsort(flat, stable=True)[:k]] = True
    return flat_mask.reshape(W_metric.shape)


# ==============================================================================
# EDITABLE REGION START
# ==============================================================================

class LayerPruner:
    """Default: remove the smallest weights, compared over the whole matrix.

    Weight-only and calibration-blind: it never looks at `scaler_row` or `H`.
    """

    def prune(self, W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta):
        W_metric = torch.abs(W)
        mask = select_by_metric(W_metric, cfg["sparsity"], cfg["prune_n"],
                                cfg["prune_m"], per_output_row=False)
        return mask, None

# ==============================================================================
# EDITABLE REGION END
# ==============================================================================

"""Driver for llm-prune-oneshot-criterion. FIXED CODE (read-only context).

Run by `scripts/prune_eval.sh` in its own process group, with a RESTRICTED view
of the data directory that holds the model weights and the calibration pool only.
It imports the editable module, walks the model with the fixed pipeline, and
writes the pruned weights to `--out-dir`. It prints no result: perplexity is
produced afterwards by `mlsb_prune/evaluate.py`, a separate process that never
imports the editable module.

    python -u -m mlsb_prune.run_prune --model M --sparsity S \
        --prune-n N --prune-m M --out-dir DIR --seed 42
"""

import argparse
import sys
import traceback

import torch

from mlsb_prune import pipeline
from mlsb_prune.custom_pruner import LayerPruner


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--sparsity", type=float, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prune-n", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--prune-m", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--nsamples", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--seqlen", type=int, default=2048)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--device", default="cuda")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    device = args.device if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

    pruner = LayerPruner()

    def prune_fn(W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta, ctx):
        return pruner.prune(W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta)

    try:
        pm = pipeline.prune_model(
            args.model, args.sparsity, args.prune_n, args.prune_m, prune_fn,
            nsamples=args.nsamples, seqlen=args.seqlen, seed=args.seed,
            device=device,
        )
    except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001 -- reported, not swallowed
        print(f"PRUNE_ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", flush=True)
        traceback.print_exc()
        return 2

    run_dir = pm.save(args.out_dir)
    print(f"SAVED artifact={run_dir} layers={len(pm.layers)} "
          f"sparsity={pm.overall_sparsity():.5f}", flush=True)
    return 0

"""Sequential block-by-block pruning of an OPT model. FIXED CODE.

This is the reference repo's own driver
(`vendor/external_packages/wanda/lib/prune_opt.py:prune_wanda` /
`prune_sparsegpt`), restructured so that the part under study is a callback:

    prune_fn(name, W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta) -> (mask, W_new)

Everything else is fixed and shared by every baseline and every submission:

  * WHICH layers are pruned -- the six projections of every decoder block, and
    nothing else (`lib/prune_opt.py:107`, `:154`);
  * the calibration corpus and its sampling -- 128 random 2048-token C4-train
    windows (`lib/prune_opt.py:129`, `lib/data.py:41-60`);
  * the two calibration statistics, accumulated during ONE dense forward pass of
    the block and each computed exactly as its reference does:
      - `scaler_row[n]`  = mean over calibration batches of the per-channel
        squared activation norm, i.e. `WrappedGPT.scaler_row`
        (`lib/layerwrapper.py:31-35`);
      - `H[n, n]`        = the SparseGPT layer Hessian `(2/N) sum_b X_b X_b^T`
        (`lib/sparsegpt.py:27-38`). Note `diag(H) == 2 * scaler_row`.
  * the order in which blocks are visited, and the rule that each block is
    re-run after pruning so the next block sees the pruned activations
    (`lib/prune_opt.py:181-184`);
  * the sparsity target and the N:M pattern, which come from the setting.

PER-LAYER SPARSITY. `prune_model` accepts an optional `layer_sparsity` mapping
(and an optional `observe_fn` / `alloc_fn` pair that produces one from a DENSE
pre-pass). It is `None` by default, in which case every layer's target is the
global `sparsity` and the arithmetic on that uniform path is bit-for-bit
independent of this parameter. The non-uniform path exists for
`llm-prune-layerwise-allocation`, whose research question is how a global budget
should be distributed across layers (OWL, arXiv:2310.05175); there the GLOBAL
budget is the constraint the out-of-process evaluator re-derives, and the
per-layer figure is whatever the allocation asked for.

COMPOSED SPARSITY + QUANTISATION. `quant_bits` is `None` by default and every
task that does not pass it sees the arithmetic it saw before the parameter
existed. When it is set, each layer additionally gets the FIXED per-output-row
grid of `mlsb_quant/grid.py` (asymmetric, min-max, derived from the ORIGINAL
weight before any submitted code runs, which is the configuration
`IST-DASLab/sparsegpt` `opt.py:29-33` quantises OPT with), the callback receives
it as `meta["grid"]`, and what the callback returns must land ON that grid: the
harness converts `W_final` to integer codes (`grid.to_codes`, which raises if a
weight sits off a level), reconstructs `scale * (code - zero)` and stores the
codes. Both budgets -- the mask's sparsity and the per-weight width -- are then
enforced out of process, and the composition is the only free choice left. This
is `llm-compress-sparse-quant-composition`.

TF32 is disabled for the same reason `lib/sparsegpt.py:8-9` disables it: the
Hessian and its Cholesky are the numerically delicate part of the reference
method, and TF32 changes them.
"""

import time

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from . import data as data_mod
from . import modelio

torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False


class _Caught(Exception):
    pass


class _Catcher(nn.Module):
    """Capture the first decoder block's inputs AND every kwarg it is called with.

    Storing the kwargs verbatim (rather than naming `attention_mask`, as
    `lib/prune_opt.py:78` does) keeps this working across transformers versions
    that add or drop arguments to `OPTDecoderLayer.forward`.
    """

    def __init__(self, module, store):
        super().__init__()
        self.module = module
        self.store = store

    def forward(self, inp, **kwargs):
        # Kept on the CPU: 128 x 2048 x hidden in fp16 is ~1 GB per copy, and a
        # rendered bundle runs every setting of a group in ONE container.
        self.store["inps"].append(inp.detach().to("cpu"))
        if self.store["kwargs"] is None:
            self.store["kwargs"] = dict(kwargs)
        raise _Caught


@torch.no_grad()
def collect_block_inputs(model, batches, device):
    layers = modelio.decoder_layers(model)
    modelio.peripheral_to(model, device)
    layers[0] = layers[0].to(device)
    store = {"inps": [], "kwargs": None}
    layers[0] = _Catcher(layers[0], store)
    for batch in batches:
        try:
            model(batch.to(device))
        except _Caught:
            pass
    layers[0] = layers[0].module
    layers[0] = layers[0].cpu()
    modelio.peripheral_to(model, "cpu")
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return torch.cat(store["inps"], dim=0), (store["kwargs"] or {})


class _StatAccumulator:
    """Both reference statistics, from the same dense forward pass.

    `scaler_row` reproduces `lib/layerwrapper.py:22-35` and `H` reproduces
    `lib/sparsegpt.py:27-38`; both are running means over CALIBRATION BATCHES
    (upstream's `tmp = inp.shape[0]` is the batch dimension, which is 1), not
    over tokens, so the constants match the reference exactly.
    """

    def __init__(self, linear, want_hessian=True, want_moments=False):
        self.columns = linear.weight.shape[1]
        self.dev = linear.weight.device
        self.scaler_row = torch.zeros(self.columns, device=self.dev,
                                      dtype=torch.float32)
        self.H = (torch.zeros((self.columns, self.columns), device=self.dev,
                              dtype=torch.float32) if want_hessian else None)
        self.nsamples = 0
        # First and second per-channel activation moments, accumulated exactly as
        # DSnoT's own wrapper does (`DSnoT/lib/layerwrapper.py:47-60`) and only
        # when a task asks for them. `None` on every other task, so nothing that
        # does not use them pays for them or sees a changed number.
        self.want_moments = want_moments
        self.sum_metric_row = (torch.zeros(self.columns, device=self.dev,
                                           dtype=torch.float32)
                               if want_moments else None)
        self.mean = (torch.zeros(self.columns, device=self.dev,
                                 dtype=torch.float32) if want_moments else None)
        self.var = (torch.zeros(self.columns, device=self.dev,
                                dtype=torch.float32) if want_moments else None)
        self.ntokens = 0

    def add(self, inp):
        if inp.dim() == 2:
            inp = inp.unsqueeze(0)
        tmp = inp.shape[0]
        if inp.dim() == 3:
            inp = inp.reshape(-1, inp.shape[-1])
        inp = inp.t()                                   # [n, tokens]
        if self.want_moments:
            # `layerwrapper.py:47-53`: a token-count-weighted running mean of the
            # per-batch mean and of the per-batch variance. Note the variance is
            # a mean of WITHIN-batch variances, not the pooled variance -- that
            # is what the released code computes and what its numbers came from.
            xm = inp.type(torch.float32)
            mean_inp = torch.mean(xm, dim=1)
            var_inp = torch.var(xm, dim=1, unbiased=False)
            num_inp = xm.shape[1]
            if self.ntokens == 0:
                self.mean = mean_inp
                self.var = var_inp
            else:
                d = float(self.ntokens + num_inp)
                self.var = (self.var * self.ntokens + var_inp * num_inp) / d
                self.mean = (self.mean * self.ntokens + mean_inp * num_inp) / d
            self.ntokens += num_inp
        scale = self.nsamples / (self.nsamples + tmp)
        self.scaler_row *= scale
        if self.H is not None:
            self.H *= scale
        if self.want_moments:
            self.sum_metric_row *= scale
        self.nsamples += tmp
        x = inp.type(torch.float32)
        self.scaler_row += torch.norm(x, p=2, dim=1) ** 2 / self.nsamples
        if self.want_moments:
            # `layerwrapper.py:60`
            self.sum_metric_row += torch.sum(x, dim=1) / self.nsamples
        if self.H is not None:
            xh = float(2.0 / self.nsamples) ** 0.5 * x
            self.H += xh.matmul(xh.t())

    def moments(self):
        if not self.want_moments:
            return None
        return {"mean": self.mean, "var": self.var,
                "sum_metric_row": self.sum_metric_row,
                "ntokens": self.ntokens, "nsamples": self.nsamples}

    def free(self):
        self.scaler_row = None
        self.H = None
        self.sum_metric_row = None
        self.mean = None
        self.var = None


@torch.no_grad()
def observe_dense(model, layers, inps, kwargs, observe_fn, device, *,
                  want_hessian=True, progress=True):
    """One DENSE walk of the decoder, calling `observe_fn` once per BLOCK.

    Nothing is modified: each block is run once, its two calibration statistics
    are accumulated exactly as the pruning walk accumulates them, `observe_fn` is
    called with the whole block, and the block's own output feeds the next block.
    This is the first of OWL's two passes (`OWL/lib/prune_all.py:884-951`), which
    derives the allocation from the UNPRUNED model before any weight is removed.

    The granularity is the block rather than the linear because that is the
    granularity OWL's own statistic is defined at: it concatenates the metric of
    every projection in a Transformer block before counting outliers
    (`OWL/lib/prune_all.py:941`, `:947`), and its Appendix C measures the
    per-linear variant at 86.285 against 24.55 for the per-block one. An
    allocation that wants per-linear sparsities still returns them; only the
    OBSERVATION is per block.

    Returns a list of `(meta, summary)` in visit order, one entry per block.
    """
    records = []
    for i in range(len(layers)):
        layer = layers[i].to(device)
        subset = modelio.find_target_linears(layer)
        accs = {name: _StatAccumulator(lin, want_hessian)
                for name, lin in subset.items()}
        handles = []
        for name, lin in subset.items():
            def hook(_mod, inp, _out, name=name):
                accs[name].add(inp[0].data)
            handles.append(lin.register_forward_hook(hook))
        outs = torch.empty_like(inps)
        for j in range(inps.shape[0]):
            outs[j] = layer(inps[j].unsqueeze(0).to(device), **kwargs)[0].to("cpu")
        for h in handles:
            h.remove()

        block = {}
        meta = {"block": i, "layers": {}}
        for name, lin in subset.items():
            m, n = int(lin.weight.shape[0]), int(lin.weight.shape[1])
            block[name] = {"W": lin.weight.data.clone().float(),
                           "scaler_row": accs[name].scaler_row,
                           "H": accs[name].H}
            meta["layers"][name] = {"name": f"decoder.{i}.{name}", "block": i,
                                    "layer": name, "m": m, "n": n,
                                    "numel": m * n}
        rec = observe_fn(block, meta)
        records.append((meta, rec))
        for name in list(block):
            block[name] = None
        del block
        for name in subset:
            accs[name].free()
        del accs
        layers[i] = layer.cpu()
        del layer
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        inps, outs = outs, inps
        del outs
        if progress:
            print(f"TRAIN_METRICS pass=observe block={i + 1}/{len(layers)}",
                  flush=True)
    return records


def resolve_layer_sparsity(layer_sparsity, name, sparsity):
    """The target for one layer. `None` reproduces the uniform path exactly."""
    if layer_sparsity is None:
        return float(sparsity)
    if name not in layer_sparsity:
        raise ValueError(f"the allocation has no entry for {name}")
    val = float(layer_sparsity[name])
    if not (0.0 <= val <= 1.0) or val != val:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: allocated sparsity {val} is outside [0, 1]")
    return val


@torch.no_grad()
def prune_model(model_name, sparsity, prune_n, prune_m, prune_fn, *,
                nsamples=128, seqlen=2048, seed=0, device="cuda",
                progress=True, want_hessian=True, ctx=None,
                observe_fn=None, alloc_fn=None, global_tol=None,
                calibration_fn=None, want_moments=False,
                quant_bits=None, quant_sym=False):
    """Prune every target linear of every decoder block. Returns PrunedModel.

    `observe_fn`/`alloc_fn` are the LAYER-ALLOCATION hook and are `None` for every
    task that does not use them; on that path the per-layer target is the global
    `sparsity` for every layer and the arithmetic is unchanged.

    `calibration_fn(tokenizer, nsamples, seqlen, seed) -> list[LongTensor]`
    replaces the fixed C4 draw and is likewise `None` by default.

    `quant_bits` turns on the COMPOSED budget described in this module's header;
    it is `None` by default and on that path no grid is built, `meta` carries no
    `"grid"`, and the artifact is the ordinary weight-and-mask one.
    """
    model_dir = data_mod.model_dir(model_name)
    tokenizer = modelio.load_tokenizer(model_dir)
    model = modelio.load_opt(model_dir)
    model.config.use_cache = False
    seqlen = min(seqlen, model.seqlen)

    if calibration_fn is None:
        batches = data_mod.calibration_batches(tokenizer, nsamples=nsamples,
                                               seqlen=seqlen, seed=seed)
    else:
        batches = calibration_fn(tokenizer, nsamples, seqlen, seed)
    pattern = f"{prune_n}:{prune_m}" if prune_n else "unstructured"
    grid_cls = None
    if quant_bits is not None:
        # Imported lazily and from the QUANTISATION sub-runtime on purpose: the
        # grid these tasks are scored against has to be the one the llm-quant-*
        # family already verifies out of process, not a second copy of it. The
        # import is inside the function so `mlsb_prune` keeps no module-level
        # dependency on `mlsb_quant` for the tasks that never quantise.
        from mlsb_quant.grid import Grid as grid_cls  # noqa: N813
    print(f"SETUP model={model_name} sparsity={sparsity:.4f} pattern={pattern} "
          f"calib={len(batches)}x{seqlen} seed={seed} "
          f"bits={'-' if quant_bits is None else int(quant_bits)}", flush=True)

    inps, kwargs = collect_block_inputs(model, batches, device)
    kwargs = {k: (v.to(device) if torch.is_tensor(v) else v) for k, v in kwargs.items()}

    pm = PrunedModel(model_name, sparsity, prune_n, prune_m,
                     quant_bits=quant_bits, quant_sym=quant_sym)
    layers = modelio.decoder_layers(model)

    layer_sparsity = None
    if observe_fn is not None or alloc_fn is not None:
        if observe_fn is None or alloc_fn is None:
            raise ValueError("observe_fn and alloc_fn must be given together")
        t_obs = time.time()
        inps0 = inps.clone()
        records = observe_dense(model, layers, inps, kwargs, observe_fn, device,
                                want_hessian=want_hessian, progress=progress)
        inps = inps0
        layer_sparsity = alloc_fn(records, float(sparsity))
        if not isinstance(layer_sparsity, dict):
            raise ValueError("the allocation must be a dict "
                             f"{{name: sparsity}}, got {type(layer_sparsity)}")
        pm.extra["observe_seconds"] = round(time.time() - t_obs, 2)
        pm.extra["allocation"] = {k: float(v) for k, v in layer_sparsity.items()}
        print("ALLOC " + " ".join(
            f"{k}={float(v):.4f}" for k, v in sorted(layer_sparsity.items())),
            flush=True)

    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(len(layers)):
        layer = layers[i].to(device)
        subset = modelio.find_target_linears(layer)

        accs = {name: _StatAccumulator(lin, want_hessian, want_moments)
                for name, lin in subset.items()}
        handles = []
        for name, lin in subset.items():
            def hook(_mod, inp, _out, name=name):
                accs[name].add(inp[0].data)
            handles.append(lin.register_forward_hook(hook))
        outs = torch.empty_like(inps)                   # on the CPU, like inps
        for j in range(inps.shape[0]):
            outs[j] = layer(inps[j].unsqueeze(0).to(device), **kwargs)[0].to("cpu")
        for h in handles:
            h.remove()

        for name, lin in subset.items():
            rec_name = f"decoder.{i}.{name}"
            W = lin.weight.data.clone().float()
            meta = {"name": rec_name, "block": i, "layer": name,
                    "m": int(W.shape[0]), "n": int(W.shape[1]),
                    "seed": seed, "model": model_name}
            if want_moments:
                meta["stats"] = accs[name].moments()
            target = resolve_layer_sparsity(layer_sparsity, rec_name, sparsity)
            cfg = {"sparsity": target, "prune_n": int(prune_n),
                   "prune_m": int(prune_m)}
            grid = None
            if grid_cls is not None:
                # From a PRISTINE copy: a submission may modify `W` in place
                # (SparseGPT's own loop does), and the grid the evaluator
                # re-derives comes from the untouched checkpoint.
                grid = grid_cls(W.clone(), int(quant_bits), bool(quant_sym))
                meta["grid"] = grid
                cfg["bits"] = int(quant_bits)
                cfg["sym"] = bool(quant_sym)
                cfg["maxq"] = float(grid.maxq)
            out = prune_fn(W, accs[name].scaler_row, accs[name].H, cfg, meta, ctx)
            mask, W_new, perm = _normalise(out, W, rec_name)
            W_final = W_new.masked_fill(mask, 0.0)
            codes = None
            if grid is not None:
                # Raises unless every entry already sits on a level: the
                # submission chooses the codes, the harness never rounds for it.
                codes = grid.to_codes(W_final, rec_name)
                W_final = grid.dequantize(codes)
                # `zero` is an integer, so the removed weights land on the exact
                # 0.0 level; check it rather than assume it.
                if bool(mask.any()) and not bool((W_final[mask] == 0).all().item()):
                    raise ValueError(f"PRUNE_BUDGET: {rec_name}: a removed weight "
                                     f"does not reconstruct to zero on the grid")
            ok, msg = check_layer_budget(rec_name, W_final, mask, target,
                                         prune_n, prune_m, perm)
            if not ok:
                raise ValueError(f"PRUNE_BUDGET: {msg}")
            lin.weight.data = W_final.to(lin.weight.dtype)
            pm.add(rec_name, lin.weight.data, mask, perm, codes=codes)
            accs[name].free()
            meta.pop("grid", None)
            del W, W_new, W_final, mask, grid, codes
        del accs
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()

        # Re-run the block so the next one sees pruned activations
        # (lib/prune_opt.py:181-184).
        for j in range(inps.shape[0]):
            outs[j] = layer(inps[j].unsqueeze(0).to(device), **kwargs)[0].to("cpu")
        layers[i] = layer.cpu()
        del layer
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        inps, outs = outs, inps
        if progress:
            print(f"TRAIN_METRICS block={i + 1}/{len(layers)} "
                  f"elapsed={time.time() - t0:.1f}s "
                  f"sparsity={pm.overall_sparsity():.4f}", flush=True)

    if global_tol is not None:
        ok, msg = check_global_budget(pm.overall_sparsity(), sparsity, global_tol)
        if not ok:
            raise ValueError(f"PRUNE_BUDGET: {msg}")
    pm.extra["prune_seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
    pm.extra["nsamples"] = len(batches)
    pm.extra["seqlen"] = seqlen
    pm.extra["seed"] = seed
    print(f"DONE pruning in {pm.extra['prune_seconds']:.1f}s "
          f"sparsity={pm.overall_sparsity():.4f}", flush=True)
    return pm


def _normalise(out, W, name):
    """Validate what a submission returned, before it is applied.

    A 2-tuple `(mask, W_new)` is the ordinary contract. A 3-tuple
    `(mask, W_new, perm)` additionally declares the input-channel ordering the
    N:M groups are cut in, which only `llm-prune-nm-selection` offers; every
    other task returns two values and `perm` is `None`.
    """
    if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) and len(out) == 3:
        mask, W_new, perm = out
    elif isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) and len(out) == 2:
        mask, W_new = out
        perm = None
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: prune() must return a (mask, W_new) pair or a "
                         f"(mask, W_new, perm) triple, got {type(out)}")
    if not torch.is_tensor(mask):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: mask must be a torch tensor, got {type(mask)}")
    if tuple(mask.shape) != tuple(W.shape):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: mask shape {tuple(mask.shape)} != "
                         f"{tuple(W.shape)}")
    mask = mask.to(device=W.device).bool()
    if W_new is None:
        W_new = W
    else:
        if not torch.is_tensor(W_new):
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: W_new must be a torch tensor or None")
        if tuple(W_new.shape) != tuple(W.shape):
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: W_new shape {tuple(W_new.shape)} != "
                             f"{tuple(W.shape)}")
        W_new = W_new.to(device=W.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    if not torch.isfinite(W_new).all():
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: W_new contains non-finite values")
    if perm is not None:
        perm = perm.to(device=W.device)
    return mask, W_new, perm

"""The pruned-weight artifact and the sparsity-budget check. FIXED CODE.

The pruning process writes exactly two files into its run directory:

    pruned.safetensors    per pruned linear, two entries: `w/<name>`, the fp16
                          weight, and `m/<name>`, its removal mask bit-packed
                          into uint8 (1 bit per weight, so ~6% of the weights'
                          own size)
    prune_manifest.json   what ran, and per-layer diagnostics (informational only)

COMPOSED SPARSITY + QUANTISATION (optional, `quant_bits` is `None` by default and
nothing below changes on that path). A task whose question is how sparsification
and quantisation should be COMPOSED (`llm-compress-sparse-quant-composition`)
constrains BOTH budgets at once, so the artifact stores the integer GRID CODE of
every weight rather than its float value:

    pruned.safetensors    `c/<name>`, the uint8 code of every weight on the fixed
                          per-output-row grid, and `m/<name>` as above. `w/` is
                          NOT written -- storing a float would let a submission
                          keep a weight off the declared grid, which is exactly
                          the budget being spent.

The grid itself is `mlsb_quant/grid.py`'s: per output row, asymmetric, min-max,
derived by fixed code from the ORIGINAL weight before any submitted code runs
(a port of `vendor/external_packages/gptq/quant.py:36-108`, which is the
configuration `IST-DASLab/sparsegpt` `opt.py:29-33` runs OPT with). The
evaluator re-derives it from the pinned checkpoint and reconstructs
`W = scale * (code - zero)`, so "every weight really is on the declared
`quant_bits`-bit grid" is structural rather than a tolerance check. `zero` is an
integer, so 0.0 is always a grid point and a removed weight reconstructs to
exactly zero.

THE BUDGET IS THE MASK, NOT THE ZEROS. The mask is stored, and checked, because
"count the zeros in the final weight" is the wrong question: a method may
legitimately write a zero into a position it did not remove. SparseGPT does
exactly that -- `lib/sparsegpt.py:56` sets `W[:, dead] = 0` for every input
channel whose calibration activation is identically zero, and OPT's `fc2` reads
a post-ReLU activation, so those channels are real (measured: 10.0% of block 1's
`fc2` inputs over 65k calibration tokens, 41% over 256). Counting them as spent
budget makes the guard fire on the published method, which is a bug wearing a
guard's clothes. So the evaluator checks that the MASK meets the budget and that
the weights are actually zero wherever the mask says so; extra zeros beyond the
mask are allowed and are only ever self-harming.

The evaluator is a SEPARATE process that never imports this module (see
`evaluate.py`, which is deliberately standalone so it can run under `python -P`).
It re-derives every quantity it checks from the saved tensors, so nothing in the
manifest can buy a submission anything.

`check_layer_budget` below is the driver-side copy of that check: it is a
fail-fast courtesy so a submission that misses the budget gets a clear message
instead of a silent rejection twenty minutes later. The evaluator's copy is the
authoritative one; both are held to the same constants, which live here and are
imported by nothing that a submission can edit.
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import torch

# Absolute tolerance on the per-layer sparsity, both directions.
#   lower bound  -- a pruner that under-prunes is not solving the task;
#   upper bound  -- keeps the per-layer budget UNIFORM. Redistributing sparsity
#                   across layers is a different research question (OWL,
#                   arXiv:2310.05175) and is deliberately not available here.
SPARSITY_TOL = 0.01

# Absolute tolerance on the GLOBAL sparsity, used by the tasks whose research
# question IS the per-layer allocation (`llm-prune-layerwise-allocation`). There
# the per-layer figure is the submission's own choice and only the global budget
# is a constraint, so it is held far tighter than the per-layer tolerance above:
# the whole point of the task is that a method may move sparsity between layers,
# and a loose global bound would let it move sparsity out of the model entirely.
#
# The number is TWICE THE ROUNDING ENVELOPE, not a round figure. A per-output-row
# pruner removes `int(n * s)` of each row, so it always rounds DOWN and the
# per-layer deficit is at most `1/n`; the parameter-weighted mean of those
# deficits is at most `1/min(n)`, which on the model this task prunes is
# 1/4096 = 0.00024. Anything looser is free under-pruning: at 0.002 a submission
# could aim at `s - 0.0015`, keep 0.15% more weights than every baseline, and
# still pass.
GLOBAL_SPARSITY_TOL = 0.0005

ARTIFACT = "pruned.safetensors"
MANIFEST = "prune_manifest.json"


def pack_mask(mask):
    """Bit-pack a bool mask into uint8, row-major. Mirrored in evaluate.py."""
    import numpy as np
    flat = mask.detach().to(torch.bool).cpu().reshape(-1).numpy()
    return torch.from_numpy(np.packbits(flat))


def unpack_mask(packed, shape):
    import numpy as np
    n = int(shape[0]) * int(shape[1])
    bits = np.unpackbits(packed.cpu().numpy().astype("uint8"))[:n]
    return torch.from_numpy(bits.astype(bool)).reshape(shape)


def nm_violations(mask, prune_n: int, prune_m: int, perm=None) -> int:
    """Number of (row, m-column-group) blocks holding fewer than `prune_n` zeros.

    The N:M convention is the reference implementation's: groups are `prune_m`
    CONSECUTIVE input channels, independently per output row
    (`vendor/external_packages/wanda/lib/prune_opt.py:114-117`,
    `lib/sparsegpt.py:94-96`). Counted on the MASK, per the note above.

    `perm` reorders the input channels before the groups are cut, which is the
    "channel reallocation" of RIA (Zhang et al., ICLR 2024, `lib/prune.py:277-288`
    and `:378-380`): the groups are then `prune_m` channels that are consecutive
    IN THE PERMUTED ORDER, and the mask stored in the original order is generally
    not N:M by itself. Tasks that do not offer a permutation pass `None` and get
    the consecutive-channel convention unchanged.
    """
    if prune_n <= 0:
        return 0
    n = mask.shape[1]
    if n % prune_m:
        raise ValueError(f"in_features {n} is not a multiple of {prune_m}")
    if perm is not None:
        mask = mask[:, perm]
    groups = mask.reshape(-1, prune_m).sum(dim=1)
    return int((groups < prune_n).sum().item())


def check_permutation(perm, n: int):
    """Return (ok, message). A permutation must be exactly a reordering of [0, n)."""
    if perm is None:
        return True, ""
    if not torch.is_tensor(perm):
        return False, f"the permutation must be a torch tensor, got {type(perm)}"
    if perm.dtype not in (torch.int16, torch.int32, torch.int64):
        return False, f"the permutation must be an integer tensor, got {perm.dtype}"
    if perm.dim() != 1 or perm.numel() != n:
        return False, (f"the permutation must have exactly {n} entries, got "
                       f"{tuple(perm.shape)}")
    srt = torch.sort(perm.to(torch.int64).cpu())[0]
    if not bool(torch.equal(srt, torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int64))):
        return False, "the permutation is not a bijection of the input channels"
    return True, ""


def layer_stats(W, mask, prune_n: int, prune_m: int, perm=None) -> dict:
    removed = int(mask.sum().item())
    return {
        "numel": int(mask.numel()),
        "removed": removed,
        "zeros": int((W == 0).sum().item()),
        "sparsity": removed / max(mask.numel(), 1),
        "nm_violations": nm_violations(mask, prune_n, prune_m, perm),
        "finite": bool(torch.isfinite(W).all().item()),
        "mask_applied": bool((W[mask] == 0).all().item()) if removed else True,
    }


def check_layer_budget(name: str, W, mask, sparsity: float, prune_n: int,
                       prune_m: int, perm=None):
    """Return (ok, message). Applied to the FINAL weight and mask of one layer."""
    ok, msg = check_permutation(perm, mask.shape[1])
    if not ok:
        return False, f"{name}: {msg}"
    st = layer_stats(W, mask, prune_n, prune_m, perm)
    if not st["finite"]:
        return False, f"{name}: weight is not finite"
    if not st["mask_applied"]:
        return False, f"{name}: the weight is non-zero where the mask removes it"
    if st["sparsity"] < sparsity - SPARSITY_TOL:
        return False, (f"{name}: sparsity {st['sparsity']:.4f} is below the "
                       f"required {sparsity:.4f} (tol {SPARSITY_TOL})")
    if st["sparsity"] > sparsity + SPARSITY_TOL:
        return False, (f"{name}: sparsity {st['sparsity']:.4f} exceeds "
                       f"{sparsity:.4f}+{SPARSITY_TOL}; the per-layer budget is "
                       f"uniform and fixed")
    if st["nm_violations"]:
        where = ("input channels" if perm is None
                 else "input channels IN THE ORDER THE PERMUTATION DECLARES")
        return False, (f"{name}: {st['nm_violations']} groups of {prune_m} "
                       f"consecutive {where} hold fewer than {prune_n} zeros")
    return True, ""


def check_global_budget(overall: float, sparsity: float,
                        tol: float = GLOBAL_SPARSITY_TOL):
    """Return (ok, message) for the model-wide sparsity. Mirrored in evaluate.py."""
    if overall < sparsity - tol:
        return False, (f"global sparsity {overall:.5f} is below the required "
                       f"{sparsity:.5f} (tol {tol})")
    if overall > sparsity + tol:
        return False, (f"global sparsity {overall:.5f} exceeds "
                       f"{sparsity:.5f}+{tol}")
    return True, ""


class PrunedModel:
    """The artifact: fp16 weights for every pruned linear, plus a manifest."""

    def __init__(self, model_name: str, sparsity: float, prune_n: int, prune_m: int,
                 quant_bits=None, quant_sym: bool = False):
        self.model_name = model_name
        self.sparsity = float(sparsity)
        self.prune_n = int(prune_n)
        self.prune_m = int(prune_m)
        # `None` is the ordinary pruning-only artifact and is the default, so
        # every task that predates the composed family writes exactly the file
        # it wrote before.
        self.quant_bits = None if quant_bits is None else int(quant_bits)
        self.quant_sym = bool(quant_sym)
        self.tensors = {}
        self.layers = {}
        self.extra = {}

    def add(self, name: str, W, mask, perm=None, codes=None):
        if self.quant_bits is None:
            if codes is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{name}: codes given but the artifact is not "
                                 f"quantised")
            self.tensors[f"w/{name}"] = W.detach().to(torch.float16).contiguous().cpu()
        else:
            if codes is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{name}: a quantised artifact stores codes, "
                                 f"not weights")
            maxq = 2 ** self.quant_bits - 1
            lo, hi = int(codes.min().item()), int(codes.max().item())
            if lo < 0 or hi > maxq:
                raise ValueError(f"{name}: code range [{lo}, {hi}] leaves the "
                                 f"{self.quant_bits}-bit grid [0, {maxq}]")
            self.tensors[f"c/{name}"] = codes.detach().to(torch.uint8).contiguous().cpu()
        self.tensors[f"m/{name}"] = pack_mask(mask)
        if perm is not None:
            self.tensors[f"p/{name}"] = perm.detach().to(torch.int32).cpu()
        self.layers[name] = layer_stats(W, mask, self.prune_n, self.prune_m, perm)

    def overall_sparsity(self) -> float:
        r = sum(v["removed"] for v in self.layers.values())
        n = sum(v["numel"] for v in self.layers.values())
        return r / max(n, 1)

    def save(self, run_dir):
        from safetensors.torch import save_file

        run_dir = Path(run_dir)
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_file(self.tensors, str(run_dir / ARTIFACT))
        manifest = {
            "model_name": self.model_name,
            "sparsity": self.sparsity,
            "prune_n": self.prune_n,
            "prune_m": self.prune_m,
            "quant_bits": self.quant_bits,
            "quant_sym": self.quant_sym,
            "overall_sparsity": self.overall_sparsity(),
            "layers": self.layers,
            "extra": self.extra,
        }
        (run_dir / MANIFEST).write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=1))
        return run_dir

"""Model loading and the set of linear layers this family prunes. FIXED CODE.

Mirrors the reference repo's OPT pipeline
(`vendor/external_packages/wanda/main_opt.py:get_llm` and
`lib/prune_opt.py:find_layers` / `prune_wanda`). Embeddings, LayerNorms, the
positional table and the LM head are never pruned: `find_layers(layer)` is called
per decoder block and only ever returns the six projections inside it
(`lib/prune_opt.py:107`, `:154`), which is what the published numbers measure.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# The six projections in an OPT decoder block. `find_layers` returns them in
# module-declaration order; we fix the order explicitly so the artifact's record
# set is deterministic.
TARGET_LINEARS = ("self_attn.k_proj", "self_attn.v_proj", "self_attn.q_proj",
                  "self_attn.out_proj", "fc1", "fc2")


def load_opt(model_path, dtype=torch.float16):
    """Load an OPT checkpoint without paying for weight init (main_opt.py:get_llm)."""
    from transformers import OPTForCausalLM

    def skip(*args, **kwargs):
        pass

    saved = (nn.init.kaiming_uniform_, nn.init.uniform_, nn.init.normal_)
    nn.init.kaiming_uniform_, nn.init.uniform_, nn.init.normal_ = skip, skip, skip
    try:
        model = OPTForCausalLM.from_pretrained(str(model_path), torch_dtype=dtype)
    finally:
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_, nn.init.uniform_, nn.init.normal_ = saved
    # main_opt.py:get_llm sets `model.seqlen = model.config.max_position_embeddings`
    # (2048 for every OPT checkpoint), which is the block length both the
    # calibration windows and the perplexity evaluation use.
    model.seqlen = model.config.max_position_embeddings
    model.eval()
    return model


def load_tokenizer(model_path):
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
    return AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(model_path), use_fast=False)


def decoder_layers(model):
    return model.model.decoder.layers


def get_linear(layer, name: str) -> nn.Linear:
    mod = layer
    for part in name.split("."):
        mod = getattr(mod, part)
    return mod


def find_target_linears(layer) -> dict:
    """The pruned linears of one decoder block, keyed by dotted name."""
    out = {}
    for name in TARGET_LINEARS:
        mod = get_linear(layer, name)
        if not isinstance(mod, nn.Linear):
            raise TypeError(f"{name} is {type(mod)}, expected nn.Linear")
        out[name] = mod
    return out


def peripheral_to(model, device):
    """Move everything outside the decoder blocks (lib/prune_opt.py:58-92)."""
    dec = model.model.decoder
    dec.embed_tokens = dec.embed_tokens.to(device)
    dec.embed_positions = dec.embed_positions.to(device)
    for attr in ("project_in", "project_out", "final_layer_norm"):
        mod = getattr(dec, attr, None)
        if mod is not None:
            setattr(dec, attr, mod.to(device))
    return model

Sun, Liu, Bair, Kolter. "A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large
Language Models", ICLR 2024, arXiv:2306.11695.

Ported from the authors' released implementation, which is vendored in this
workspace:

  * the metric  -- `vendor/external_packages/wanda/lib/prune_opt.py:163`

"""Which weights should a one-shot sparsifier remove, and what should the ones
that survive be set to?

You design `LayerPruner.prune`. Everything else -- which layers are pruned, the
calibration corpus and its sampling, the two calibration statistics, the order in
which blocks are visited, the sparsity budget, the sparsity pattern, the storage
format and the evaluation -- is fixed and shared by every method.

WHAT THE HARNESS DOES WITH WHAT YOU RETURN
------------------------------------------
For each linear layer of each decoder block, in order, the fixed pipeline

    1. runs the calibration corpus through the block and collects, for that
       layer, `scaler_row` and `H` (below);
    2. calls `self.prune(W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta)` once;
    3. applies `W_final = W_new.masked_fill(mask, 0)` and installs it;
    4. re-runs the block, so every later block sees the activations of the
       ALREADY-PRUNED model -- your decision for layer k changes the statistics
       layer k+1 is scored on;
    5. writes the finished weights to an artifact. A separate process, which
       never imports this file, reloads that artifact, re-derives the sparsity of
       every layer, and computes the perplexity that is scored.

CONTRACT
--------
`prune(W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta) -> (mask, W_new)`

    W           float32 [m, n]  the layer's dense weight (a copy; m outputs,
                                n input channels). `y = x @ W.T`.
    scaler_row  float32 [n]     mean over calibration batches of the squared
                                l2 norm of each input channel's activations.
    H           float32 [n, n]  the layerwise second-moment matrix
                                (2/N) * sum_b X_b X_b^T over the same batches.
                                Note `torch.diag(H) == 2 * scaler_row`.
    cfg         dict            {"sparsity", "prune_n", "prune_m"} -- fixed by
                                the harness, never by you.
    meta        dict            {"name", "block", "layer", "m", "n", "seed",
                                "model"}.

    mask        bool  [m, n]    True = remove this weight.
    W_new       float32 [m, n]  what the surviving weights should be. Return
                                `None` to keep the original values; return a
                                tensor to compensate for what was removed.

Called inside `torch.no_grad()` on GPU tensors. `torch` and `math` are
available. There is no network, no evaluation data, and nothing outside this
call to write state into that the evaluator will read.

BUDGET -- the same for every method, and enforced out of process
---------------------------------------------------------------
Your mask must remove `cfg["sparsity"]` of EACH layer's weights, to within a
small tolerance in BOTH directions. You choose WHICH weights, never HOW MANY,
and never how the budget is split between layers. When `cfg["prune_n"] > 0` the
mask must additionally remove at least `prune_n` of every `prune_m` CONSECUTIVE
input channels, independently for each output row. A run that misses either
constraint on any layer produces no metric at all.

The budget is the MASK, not the zeros: the mask is stored alongside the weights
and the evaluator checks both that it meets the budget and that the weights are
genuinely zero wherever it removes one. Writing a zero into a position the mask
did not remove is allowed and only costs you accuracy.
"""

import math

import torch


# ==============================================================================
# FIXED -- selection helpers. Call them or write your own; the mask you return is
# what counts.
# ==============================================================================

def select_by_metric(W_metric, sparsity, prune_n, prune_m, per_output_row=True):
    """Remove the lowest-scoring weights under the requested pattern.

    `per_output_row=True` compares scores only among the weights feeding one
    output neuron (`sparsity` of each ROW is removed); `False` compares them
    across the whole matrix (`sparsity` of the TENSOR is removed). Both are used
    in the literature and the choice is part of the method, not of the harness.

    When `prune_n > 0` the comparison group is instead each block of `prune_m`
    consecutive input channels within a row, and `per_output_row` is ignored.

    In every case EXACTLY the budgeted number of weights is removed from each
    group, with ties broken by index. That matters: a metric can be exactly zero
    for a whole input channel -- OPT's `fc2` reads a post-ReLU activation, so a
    channel that never fires has zero activation norm -- and a plain
    `metric <= threshold` rule would then remove an unbounded number of extra
    weights and miss the budget.
    """
    W_mask = torch.zeros_like(W_metric, dtype=torch.bool)
    if prune_n > 0:
        for ii in range(0, W_metric.shape[1], prune_m):
            tmp = W_metric[:, ii:(ii + prune_m)].float()
            idx = torch.topk(tmp, prune_n, dim=1, largest=False)[1]
            W_mask.scatter_(1, ii + idx, True)
        return W_mask
    if per_output_row:
        order = torch.sort(W_metric, dim=-1, stable=True)[1]
        keep = int(W_metric.shape[1] * sparsity)
        W_mask.scatter_(1, order[:, :keep], True)
        return W_mask
    flat = W_metric.flatten().float()
    k = int(flat.numel() * sparsity)
    flat_mask = torch.zeros_like(flat, dtype=torch.bool)
    if k > 0:
        flat_mask[torch.argsort(flat, stable=True)[:k]] = True
    return flat_mask.reshape(W_metric.shape)


# ==============================================================================
# EDITABLE REGION START
# ==============================================================================


class LayerPruner:
    """Wanda: |W_ij| * ||X_j||_2, compared within each output row."""

    def prune(self, W, scaler_row, H, cfg, meta):
        W_metric = torch.abs(W) * torch.sqrt(scaler_row.reshape((1, -1)))
        mask = select_by_metric(W_metric, cfg["sparsity"], cfg["prune_n"],
                               cfg["prune_m"], per_output_row=True)
        return mask, None

# ==============================================================================
# EDITABLE REGION END
# ==============================================================================

baselines.name: RIA (Zhang et al., 2024)
baselines.docstring:
RIA baseline for llm-prune-oneshot-criterion.

Zhang, Bai, Lin, Zhao, Hou, Cannistraci. "Plug-and-Play: An Efficient
Post-training Pruning Method for Large Language Models", ICLR 2024
(OpenReview id Tr0lPx9woF). The method has no arXiv version; the citation is the
ICLR 2024 proceedings paper.

Ported from the authors' released implementation, vendored at
`vendor/external_packages/RIA-pruning` (commit 7bc55b0):

  * the metric -- `lib/prune.py:239`, verbatim:

        W_metric = (torch.abs(W)/torch.sum(torch.abs(W), dim=0)
                    + torch.abs(W)/torch.sum(torch.abs(W), dim=1).reshape(-1, 1)) \
                   * (torch.sqrt(wrapped_layers[name].scaler_row.reshape((1,-1))))**args.a

    i.e. Relative Importance (paper Eq. 2) times the activation term raised to
    `a` (paper Eq. 3). `--a` defaults to **0.5** (`main.py:45`), which the paper
    selects in its Figure 9 sweep ("we select a=0.5 in the main text to execute
    all the evaluations").
  * the comparison group -- LAYER-WISE. `lib/prune.py:403-410` puts the
    per-output-neuron group behind `--per_outneuron`, which `main.py:51`
    declares `store_true` and therefore defaults to False, so the released
    default takes a single threshold over the whole matrix. This differs from
    Wanda's group, and the difference is part of the published method.
  * the N:M branch -- `lib/prune.py:394-401` ("Directly N:M"), `prune_n`
    smallest of every `prune_m` consecutive input channels.

DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED: heuristic channel reallocation and linear sum
assignment (`--reallocation` / `--lsa`, `lib/prune.py:243-385`). Those permute
input channels so that the N:M groups are formed over a REORDERED set of
columns; the resulting mask is not N:M with respect to consecutive columns, and
using it would change the sparsity pattern the harness fixes for every method.
The paper reports them as separate columns ("2:4+CP") and applies them to Wanda
and SparseGPT as well, so they are a method-agnostic post-process rather than
part of the RIA score..
